page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the compute-optimized c2d family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports hardware-accelerated instructions such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 support. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In performance evaluations, the c2d-standard-8 exhibits strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers with a stress-ng single-core score of 2865.09. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range, scoring 11559.23 in stress-ng and 6531.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is measured at 553.27 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, and approximately 46.79 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform at average levels, with a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 28.36 GB/sec and a Passmark CPU encryption score of 9352.1. Database operations and web serving throughput also align with mid-tier expectations, demonstrating a Redis SET throughput of 8.77 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 10.68 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource profile for workloads requiring dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources without the overhead of local storage or specialized GPU hardware. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for general-purpose compute tasks, web serving, and software compilation. Given its strong single-core performance and average multi-core scaling, this instance is appropriate for application servers, moderate database operations, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks, such as prompt processing and text generation using small language models.
